Australian shares set for best day since mid-June as Democrats' win sparks rally
sum: Australian shares were on track for their best session since mid-June on Thursday, mirroring a rally in global equities as Democrats' sweep of the US midterm elections boosted risk appetite and offset a sharp fall in National Australia Bank.
The S&P/ASX 200 index advanced 1.8% to 8,991.30 by 0102 GMT, putting it on course for its strongest daily gain since June 12. The index had closed 0.6% lower on Wednesday.

Gains were broad-based, with nine of 12 sectors trading higher after global markets rallied overnight on expectations that Democrats' control of both chambers of Congress would reduce policy uncertainty.
The election result also fuelled hopes that a shift in power away from Republicans could accelerate efforts to end the US-Israeli conflict with Iran, helping drive oil prices down more than 8%.
In Sydney, miners surged 6.1% and were set for their best day since early April 2025 after copper and iron ore prices rebounded overnight. Rio Tinto and BHP rose more than 4% each.
Gold stocks jumped more than 9% after bullion prices surged overnight, helped by a weaker US dollar.

Technology stocks soared 8.2%, led by a more than 40% surge in NextDC after the data-centre operator described a stake build by entities linked to Goodman Group and Digital Realty as "opportunistic" and said it had received no takeover proposal.

sum: The Australian sharemarket has fallen following a tech sell-off in the United States and ahead of an expected interest rate hike in Australia.
The benchmark S&P/ASX200 index on Monday dropped 51.6 points, or 0.58 per cent, while the broader All Ordinaries shed 48.2 points, or 0.53 per cent, to 8977.2.
The Australian dollar was buying US70.22¢, down from 70.33 US cents on Friday at 5pm.

Westpac was the only bank to register a gain on Monday. Its shares closed up 1 per cent after reporting a $6.8 billion full-year profit, saying it expects interest rates to remain “elevated” into 2027 and house prices to fall by as much as 11 per cent by next March.

Westpac’s profit in the year to September was down 1 per cent from the previous year. The bank’s net interest margin – a key measure of profitability – fell by 3 percentage points to 1.86 per cent for the second half of 2026 as lending competition remained strong and more customer accounts qualified for savings bonus rates. sum: Australia’s sharemarket has stumbled at the finish line but has closed the week higher as a rebound in recently neglected bank stocks continues.
The S&P/ASX200 rose 1.3 per cent for the week after rising 16.3 points on Friday, or 0.2 per cent, to 8908.1, while the broader All Ordinaries gained 12.8 points, or 0.14 per cent, to 9025.4.

The heavyweight financials sector provided much of the momentum, as investors sought safety in Australia’s banks after US tech earnings raised questions about artificial intelligence’s projected returns.
“Wall Street turned decidedly sour as investors penalised tech heavyweights for aggressive spending and elusive pay-offs,” Moomoo chief market strategist Tapas Strickland said.

The mining sector, a large part of the local market, had a mixed day. BHP edged up 0.1 per cent, while Fortescue slid 2.2. Mining giant Rio Tinto slumped 1.6 per cent after an incident at its Oyu Tolgoi copper mine in Mongolia. A rockfall triggered by a seismic event on Thursday caused three workers to be injured, the company said in a statement on Friday.

Most of the major banks advanced as Commonwealth Bank gained 0.2 per cent, National Australia Bank gained 0.4 per cent, and ANZ Bank closed 0.2 per cent higher. Westpac, which is due to deliver its full-year results on Monday, slipped 1.1 per cent.

Shares in supermarket giant Coles plunged 7.7 per cent after the company’s first quarter sales result revealed that growth had slowed in October, and it highlighted customers were shopping around for value. It also said high fuel costs would add to its expenses, and it expected first-half supermarket profits to be flat compared with the prior period.

Why have Rio Tinto shares lost 23% since June?
sum: Rio Tinto Ltd (ASX: RIO) shares have slumped even further on Thursday afternoon.
At the time of writing, the ASX mining shares are down around 2% to $150.22 a piece.
Since hitting an all-time high in early-June, the shares have now shed 23% of their value, reversing a lot of the gains made earlier this year.
Rio Tinto's share price decline over the past four months is mostly the result of a sharp drop in iron ore prices over the same period.

Major miners like Rio Tinto are relatively resilient companies, but a large amount of the miner's cash flows from its large iron ore operations, which means the latest commodity price downturn has put incredible stress on the company's margins.

According to Trading Economics, iron ore spiked at an annual high close to US$112 per tonne in mid-May, before crashing in early June. Iron ore is now trading around a three-year low of US$90 per tonne. That's also a 7% decline over the past month and a 14% decline over the year.
The iron decline is the result of weaker Chinese steel demand, aggressive price negotiations in China, and increased global iron ore supply.

Rio Tinto reports 90.8 million tonnes: Rio Tinto stock trails EUR 78.28
sum: Rio Tinto (ISIN GB0007188757) reported 90.8 million tonnes of global iron ore sales for the third quarter of 2026, up 3 percent from a year earlier. The update dated October 14, 2026 kept full-year iron ore sales guidance at 343-366 million tonnes, according to Rio Tinto.

The quarterly release showed Pilbara iron ore sales of 85.7 million tonnes, 2 percent higher than in the third quarter of 2025. Rio Tinto said the increase reflected mine performance and port inventories, while its annual production targets for other commodities remained unchanged.

The operating mix was uneven. Copper production totaled 205,000 tonnes in the third quarter, unchanged year over year, while Oyu Tolgoi output rose 27 percent. Nine-month copper production reached 646,000 tonnes, 1 percent above the comparable 2025 period.

JPMorgan lowered its Rio Tinto target from GBp 8,100 to GBp 7,950 on October 13, 2026, while retaining a Neutral rating, according to FinanzNachrichten. The cited assessment focused on limited near-term Chinese investment stimulus and did not identify immediate positive drivers.

On October 1, 2026, Rio Tinto announced that the Bell Bay Aluminium operation would continue through 2031. On October 1, 2026, it also transferred the Argyle Pink Diamonds brand to Boodles after the final inventory transaction. On October 14, 2026, the company reported 90.8 million tonnes of third-quarter global iron ore sales and maintained its 343-366 million-tonne annual guidance.

For investors, the key contrast is between steady shipment guidance and a more cautious external valuation. Rio Tinto also reported a 29 percent year-to-date increase in Oyu Tolgoi copper production and a 33 percent year-to-date increase in lithium production in its October 14 update.

Rio Tinto was trading at EUR 78.24 at Lang & Schwarz on October 21, 2026, at 10:01 a.m. CEST, 0.05 percent below the Xetra close of October 20, 2026 at EUR 78.28. The primary listing is on the London Stock Exchange, where the shares closed at GBp 6,545.00 on October 20, 2026.

Mining stocks rally comes to abrupt halt as copper, silver prices plummet and gold slides
sum: Metals and mining stocks sold off across the board on Thursday as a US producer price report and crude oil above $105 a barrel pushed the odds of a Federal Reserve rate increase next week to about 70%, and a report that the White House copper tariff plan has stalled pulled the rug from under a metal that had set records in four straight sessions.

Comex copper for December delivery fell as much as 5.4% to $6.5160 a pound in New York, a day after settling at a record $6.8885, and was trading at $6.5220 (about $14,380 a tonne) in early afternoon, down 5.3% and just above the day’s low. Comex gold for December delivery dropped as much as 2.1% to $4,365.40 an ounce before paring the loss to 1.6% at $4,391.00, while December silver slid as much as 6.1% to $64.455 and was last at $64.575, down 5.9%. Platinum and palladium each lost more than 6%.

Copper’s drop followed a Reuters report that the White House has not decided on refined copper tariffs as officials weigh the risk of higher manufacturing costs ahead of November’s midterm elections, a possibility the market had all but priced out after traders spent the year hauling metal into US warehouses. Hedge funds are heavily long and the metal’s correlation with the S&P 500 sits at multidecade highs, leaving little cushion when the tariff premium wobbled.

Gold came under pressure from Brent crude spiking on rising tensions in the Middle East with swap traders lifting the probability of a September hike from roughly 60% earlier in the day, with consumer price figures on Friday the last major release before the Fed meets. Silver, which had outrun gold on the way up in August, fell more than four times as far as bullion, and platinum and palladium fell with it as the dollar and Treasury yields both firmed after the data.

Freeport-McMoRan, the largest listed copper producer, was down over 7% in early afternoon trade in New York, and the 15 million shares that had changed hands by then already exceeded a full day’s average volume over the past two weeks. The drop cut Freeport’s market value to $101.7 billion, and another 2% would take it back below the $100 billion mark it crossed in the August rally for the first time.

Rio Tinto PLC Stock (RIO) Closed Up by 3.06% on Aug 21: Key Drivers Unveiled
sum: Rio Tinto PLC (RIO) closed up by 3.06%. The Mineral Resources sector is up by 3.93%. The company underperformed the industry. Top 3 stocks by turnover in the sector: Freeport-McMoRan Inc (FCX) up 7.64%; Newmont Corporation (NEM) up 3.09%; Agnico Eagle Mines Ltd (AEM) up 1.90%.

The upward movement in Rio Tinto's shares alongside significant intraday volatility was primarily driven by a convergence of improving commodity sentiment, favorable institutional positioning, and constructive long-term supply dynamics. Global resource equities experienced positive momentum as institutional investors expanded portfolio allocations into cyclical, asset-backed sectors. This broader sector rotation has been fueled by growing appreciation for multi-metal producers capable of delivering strong free cash flow yields while serving as key suppliers to infrastructure and energy transition initiatives.

A core fundamental catalyst supporting market interest is the ongoing strength in Rio Tinto's operational performance following its robust first-half earnings report. The company has demonstrated strong cash generation capabilities, underpinned by solid iron ore shipments from the Pilbara region and accelerating output in its copper business. Wall Street brokerages have increasingly highlighted Rio Tinto's valuation appeal relative to major mining peers, pointing to a more favorable EV/EBITDA multiple and a manageable capital expenditure burden as key projects transition into high-margin production phases. Tactical portfolio shifts away from competitors embarking on heavy capital investment cycles have provided steady buying pressure.

On the strategic front, long-term investor confidence has been reinforced by recent agreements securing low-cost, renewable power supply for major assets, such as the Tomago aluminum smelter deal. By mitigating long-term energy transition costs and regulatory hurdles, Rio Tinto has enhanced its operational resilience. Furthermore, management commentary emphasizing natural mine depletion across global iron ore basins has highlighted potential medium-to-long-term supply deficits, reassuring investors that market pricing will remain supported over time even amidst fluctuating near-term industrial demand.

Would I invest $5,000 into Rio Tinto shares this week?
sum: Rio Tinto Ltd (ASX: RIO) has been one of the stronger performers in the mining sector over the past year.
After a run like that, it is reasonable to wonder whether much of the opportunity has already been captured.
According to CommSec, consensus earnings per share estimates stand at $12.07 in FY26 and $12.04 in FY27.
That puts the miner on a forward price-to-earnings multiple of around 14 times in both years.
I think that looks reasonable for a global mining company with substantial exposure to iron ore, aluminium and, increasingly, copper.

There is passive income to consider as well. CommSec expects fully franked dividends of $6.63 per share in FY26 and $6.62 in FY27, which would represent a forecast yield of roughly 3.9% at the current share price.
That gives investors something back while waiting for the longer-term growth story to develop.

items.t: Rio Tinto stock holds firm after a 43% profit jump
sum: Rio Tinto stock is trading with a stronger earnings backdrop after interim 2026 underlying net profit rose 43% year over year to USD 6.9 billion, or USD 4.21 per share, and the dividend increased 43% to USD 2.11.

As reported on August 6, 2026, the earnings lift came alongside a lower effective tax rate of 25% for the half, versus prior guidance for around 30%, giving investors a cleaner read on margin support.

The second number that matters is the mix. Copper and aluminum together made up 56% of first-half underlying EBITDA, while iron ore accounted for almost all of the remainder, showing how the earnings base has broadened beyond one commodity.

For investors, that mix matters because it ties the profit rebound to products with different price drivers. The same results also showed free cash flow strength, with the company highlighting a 75% increase in that measure in the first-half results coverage published on August 2, 2026.

Rio Tinto shares closed at $97.24 on August 17, 2026, up 1.63% on the session, with a market value of $122.04 billion and a 52-week range of $60.22 to $112.58. The stock has also risen 21.5% from the start of 2026, which keeps the move tied to both earnings and valuation.

Analyst consensus on the stock remains Hold, with a median target of $105.50 and an implied gap that is still modest relative to the latest close. That combination leaves the shares priced more on earnings durability than on a fresh rerating.

Rio Tinto's core portfolio still spans iron ore, aluminum, copper, diamonds and other industrial materials. The latest half-year commentary pointed to copper and aluminum as the biggest contributors to the earnings mix, which is where the market is now focusing its attention.

On 30 June, BHP shares closed trading for $59.40. When the closing bell sounded on 31 July, shares were changing hands for $60.31, up 1.5% for the month.
Rio Tinto shares went the other direction. Rio Tinto shares closed June at $172.51 and finished out July trading for $170.57 each, down 1.1%.
And Fortescue shares trailed the pack in July, closing the month down 3.3% to trade for $18.51 apiece.

Why Are Glencore (LSE:GLEN) Shares Jumping On Renewed Rio Tinto Merger Talk?
sum: - Glencore (LSE:GLEN) Basic Materials Glencore PLC (LSE:GLEN) 541.80 GBX +3.700 0.688% Last Updated at: 2026-10-27T16:37:00Z shares have surged after confirmation that merger discussions with Rio Tinto (LSE:RIO) Basic Materials Rio Tinto PLC (LSE:RIO) 6400.00 GBX +157.000 2.515% Last Updated at: 2026-10-27T16:39:00Z have restarted.
- The renewed talks revive speculation about a landmark combination between two of the world's largest diversified mining groups.
- The development has placed both companies firmly back in focus among investors tracking the value characteristics of the mining sector.

Rio Tinto has confirmed it is in discussions with Glencore regarding a potential merger, marking a return to talks that had previously been explored between the two groups. A combination of this scale would bring together two of the world's most significant diversified mining businesses, spanning commodities such as copper, coal, and other industrial metals. The renewed discussions have been closely watched given the scale of both companies' operations and the potential implications for global commodity supply chains should any transaction eventually be completed.

Glencore and Rio Tinto have both frequently featured in discussions about undervalued opportunities within the FTSE 100's resources sector, with commentators pointing to their asset bases, commodity exposure and cash generation potential relative to their market valuations. The prospect of a merger has added a fresh dimension to this value narrative, as investors consider whether a combined entity could unlock efficiencies or strategic advantages not currently reflected in either company's standalone valuation. Mining stocks have also featured prominently in broader commentary about banks and miners lifting the FTSE 100, reinforcing the sector's relevance to the current value investing conversation.

Given the early stage of the renewed discussions, there remains considerable uncertainty about whether a formal transaction will ultimately materialise, and both companies are likely to provide further updates as talks progress. Investors and analysts will be watching closely for any formal statements regarding deal structure, regulatory considerations and the strategic rationale behind combining the two businesses.

sum: Rio Tinto PLC (RIO) moved up by 3.81%. The Mineral Resources sector is up by 2.04%. The company outperformed the industry. Top 3 stocks by turnover in the sector: Hecla Mining Co (HL) up 1.67%; Freeport-McMoRan Inc (FCX) up 3.23%; Newmont Corporation (NEM) up 1.66%.

Rio Tintos upward momentum during the current session is primarily driven by a resurgence in global commodity prices, particularly iron ore and copper, following updated economic stimulus signals from major industrial hubs in Asia. As one of the worlds largest producers of base metals, any indication of increased infrastructure spending or a stabilization in construction activity directly translates to improved demand expectations for the companys core exports. The recent strength in spot prices has provided a clear tailwind for the mining giant, which maintains some of the highest margins in the industry due to its low-cost operations in the Pilbara region.

Institutional sentiment has also been bolstered by the companys recent production results. The data indicates that operational efficiencies are improving, with iron ore shipments reaching the upper end of guidance despite previous logistical challenges. Furthermore, the continued ramp-up of the Oyu Tolgoi underground copper mine is beginning to reflect more significantly in the companys growth profile. Investors are increasingly viewing the firm as a primary beneficiary of the global energy transition, as its expanding copper and lithium portfolio aligns with long-term secular trends in electrification and green technology.

From a macroeconomic perspective, a softening of the US Dollar has provided additional support for the stock. Since commodities are priced in dollars, a weaker greenback makes the companys products more affordable for international buyers, further stimulating demand. Additionally, a stabilizing interest rate environment reduces the capital expenditure pressure on large-scale mining projects and enhances the companys ability to sustain its generous dividend policy. This combination of fiscal discipline and macro tailwinds has prompted several major investment banks to revise their price forecasts upward, citing a favorable risk-reward profile compared to its diversified mining peers.
